demo_page.title: Demo walkthrough: Connection for Loved Ones — from a director's brief to a six-pager
demo_page.description: An end-to-end 12-step run of the AI agent on a client brief, Connection for Loved ones and personal devices (a mobile operator): 26 claims with sources, 5 options and a red team — 20 hits, decision D001 "Warn before the outage" — a 600-group pilot with a −3 pp threshold.
demo_page.og_title: Demo walkthrough: Connection for Loved Ones — from a director's brief to a six-pager
demo_page.k008: Demo walkthrough: Connection for Loved Ones — from a director's brief to a six-pager
demo_page.k018: A teaching brief from a client: a fictional mobile operator; some customers help loved ones stay connected, others run several numbers of their own. The planned-year goal is gross profit ≥ 285M ₽; the gap to the "no change" forecast is 6M ₽ = 12,000 extra paid months × ₽500.
demo_page.k019: A complete run: 12 steps, 3 mandatory human pauses. The registry: 26 claims — 10 facts, 8 assumptions, 4 hypotheses, 4 inferences; 4 sources (the brief, 2 AI respondents — hypotheses only, a wireframe); calculations are reproducible: economics.py and 4 formula-based Excel workbooks.
demo_page.k021: Brief to the agent (verbatim from project.json): "Your team runs the services of a fictional mobile operator. Some customers help loved ones stay connected. Others manage several numbers of their own. Decide who to help first, what exactly to change, and why the operator should invest money in it. Prepare a plan for the coming year and set a benchmark for the end of year three…"
demo_page.k022: Comparison axis: contribution to the planned-year gross profit (extra paid months × ₽500) and active groups (goal: 8,000).
demo_page.k023: Constraints: all numbers are teaching numbers set by the brief; two decisions for the lead — end of Q1 (run the pilot?) and end of Q2 (expand?); participant consents are granular: balance / payments / pay on my behalf.
demo_page.k024: Demo overview: run videos and materials

Planned-year expansion only if the effect is ≥−3 pp on exhaustion-driven restrictions [C013]. Owners of several numbers — the second wave, Q3–Q4 [C016]. Review: 2027-04-30.

help_page.title: Help — Product Factory Strategist
help_page.description: Full documentation for the Product Factory Strategist AI agent: the 12 process steps, sources S###, claims C###, decisions D###, Excel models, the six-pager, skills, subagents, MCP, environments, security and troubleshooting.
help_page.k009: 12 steps · {{N_MAPS}} knowledge cards · {{N_SKILLS}} skills · {{N_AGENTS}} subagents · {{N_HOOKS}} hooks · {{N_MCP}} MCP tools · 0 dependencies
help_page.k016: Connection for Loved Ones demo ★
help_page.k058: Key points — the whole gist in one minute
help_page.k060: Every number and conclusion: a type (fact/hypothesis/forecast/assumption/inference), grade A–D, and a source. The chain S### → C### → D### is traceable from link to decision.
help_page.k062: The agent drives: brief → sources → research → discovery → situation → options → choice → strategies → validation plan → quality review → decision → monitoring.
help_page.k064: At least three substantively distinct ones, including "do nothing" and "shut it down". A dedicated red-team subagent attacks each.
help_page.k066: projects/<slug>/ stores everything. New chat, another environment, a break — work resumes where it stopped, no repeats.
help_page.k068: 4 workbooks (unit economics, growth, cohorts, market) build in the background; the Input sheet holds parameters, the rest are formulas.
help_page.k070: An action log, grounds behind conclusions, cost in tokens and money — pfs cost, pfs next, pfs check --strict.
help_page.k072: Write in plain language as to a colleague. The agent understands three kinds of messages: a task ("why is in-app retention dropping"), answers to its questions (pick an option or reply freely) and control phrases (see below). It never asks more than three questions at once and always explains what it is missing and why it matters for the next step.
help_page.k073: A good first request names the decision to make: "Help me decide whether to launch antispam as a paid subscription; here is the brief and six months of data." A weak one ("make me a strategy") also works — the agent clarifies the decision, audience and constraints via pfs ask before spending your tokens.
help_page.k075:
PhraseWhat happens
"stop"Pause: state saved, the agent stays quiet until a new command
"clarify: …"Adjust the task; only the affected part is redone, sources are not duplicated
"redo section X"Targeted rework of a single document section
"what should I decide now"pfs next: current step, overdue decisions, stale grounds, open questions
"what's due"pfs decision due: decisions and commitments whose review date arrived
"what will this new source affect"pfs impact: which conclusions, document lines and decisions go stale
"build the six-pager"pfs calc all + pfs export --six-pager: FAQ-1…6 report and 4 Excel workbooks
"recalculate Excel"pfs calc all — workbooks rebuilt from current calcs.json
"build the report" / "build the deck"pfs export → REPORT.md; pfs export --deck → 16:9 HTML deck
"make it a doc"pfs docx file.md — Markdown to Word, dependency-free
"check the project"pfs check --strict — numbers, links, options
"how much did it cost"pfs cost — tokens and money per model

Two-step six-pager workflow (PRO-46): pfs export --six-pager builds a data pack (six_pager_pack.json/md) and a FAQ-1…6 skeleton with slots; slot text is written by the six-pager-writer subagent with the mandatory loop "write → pfs check --six-pager → 0 errors".

Full end-to-end testing guide: QUICKSTART_EN.md in the repository.
help_page.k077: Requirements: Python 3.9+ and any supported environment. No packages to install — standard library only. Secrets (Linear and other MCP keys) go to .env — it is git-ignored and not required for the basic loop.
help_page.k079: pfs new "<name>" "<the request verbatim>" creates projects/<slug>/ (sources, interviews, analysis, outputs, state.json, log.jsonl) and activates it. The agent then: classifies the scenario via routing (pfs route), asks the intake question block — up to 3 questions — writes outputs/00_brief.md and stops for your approval. That is the first of three human pauses.
help_page.k080: Switch projects with pfs use <slug>, list them with pfs list, inspect state with pfs status.
help_page.k081: Connection for Loved Ones demo: how it was made and what to look at
help_page.k082: A complete end-to-end run on a client brief — Connection for Loved Ones and personal devices (services of a fictional mobile operator): 12 steps, {{OPT_COUNT}} options, {{RT_HITS}} red-team hits (15 objections + 5 hidden assumptions), both strategies, a six-pager in 4 formats (RU/EN × MD/DOCX), {{XLSX_COUNT}} Excel workbooks, decision D001 — a 600-group pilot, check --strict: 0 errors, a 98/100 review. Project: projects/связь-для-близких-и-собственных-устройств/; interactive walkthrough: demo.html.
help_page.k083: What to look at (in order): 00_brief → 01_research_plan → 02_situation → 03_options ({{OPT_COUNT}} options + {{RT_HITS}} red-team hits) → 04/05 (strategies) → 06_validation_plan (pilot thresholds, ~8–10 weeks) → BRIEF_RESPONSE.md (the 5-part answer to the brief), REPORT.md and SIX_PAGER / SIX_PAGER_EN in .md/.docx; Excel in outputs/attachments/; the dashboard wireframe in sources/raw/; the step log is log.jsonl.
help_page.k085: Compliance check: the mandatory minimum (task · materials · research · ≥3 options with objections · both strategies · validation plan · workflow · knowledge order · continuation after a break · transparency) and the extra level (synthetic data · media · data · decisions · review · routing · subagents/hooks · MCP/CLI · robustness · portability · comparison with a chat) — all closed; the full mapping is in README and docs/COMPLIANCE.md.
help_page.k086: Mistakes along the way (honestly): market estimates from aggregators diverge ×2 — recorded as ranges [S006]; source numbering shifted during re-registration — tags re-bound and re-checked with check --strict; some C### links drifted to neighbouring claims during migration — caught by a registry audit and fixed. The human helped at three pauses: brief, option choice, decision D001 approval.
help_page.k088: The cycle is 12 steps in four double-diamond phases: Discover (1–4) → Define (5–7) → Develop (8–10) → Deliver (11–12). Each step has mandatory knowledge cards (pfs step prints them), a question block (pfs questions <step>), quality gates and an artifact. Progress shows in one line: Step N/12 · research · sources S001–S009 · next: situation. Steps 0, 6, 10 are human pauses: brief, option choice, decision approval.
help_page.k090: Input: your request verbatim. Agent: clarifies the target decision, goal, audience and format, constraints, available data — the intake question block (≤3 questions with options and a recommendation). Output: outputs/00_brief.md. Human: approves the brief — it is then fixed and can ground assumptions (like source S020 in the demo). Commands: pfs new, pfs questions intake, pfs answer "…".
help_page.k092: Input: your files and a list of public pages. Agent: registers materials — pfs source add <url|file> — dedup by URL and SHA-256 (a repeat adds nothing), extracts text from PDF/DOCX/XLSX/CSV/pages, checks the domain against the project's allowed_sources, flags embedded instruction-like phrases (data, not commands). Output: sources/S###.md + copies in sources/raw/. Commands: add/list/show/refresh; refreshing a web source compares hashes and warns on changes.
help_page.k094:
Agent: builds a plan from questions that could change the decision ("question → if yes / if no → how it affects"), extracts claims with type, grade and quote, runs calculations, prepares interviews when needed. A fact without a source cannot be stored — the tool refuses. Output: outputs/01_research_plan.md, claims.jsonl (C###), analysis/. Commands: pfs claim add, pfs data profile|cohort|funnel|stats, pfs interview guide|save, pfs media add. Gate: every key question answered with a C### or an explicitly named gap.

pfs ab --hypothesis "…" --metric "…" — A/B test design: proxy, guardrail, MDE, traffic, stop rule (PRO-71).
help_page.k096: Agent: builds personas and their jobs-to-be-done, describes user alternatives — how people solve the problem today; the discovery question block fixes the segment. AI respondents (the synthetic-respondent subagent) yield hypotheses about motives and barriers — registered with origin=synthetic and unable to prove demand. Output: the "Segments" section of 02_situation.md, transcripts in interviews/synthetic/.
help_page.k098: Agent: assembles a verifiable picture: what is known and from where (C### tags), what we do not know and why it matters, contradictions between sources. Every number in a document must carry a tag — check catches "naked" numbers. Output: outputs/02_situation.md. Gate: pfs check with zero errors.
help_page.k100: Agent: prepares at least three substantively distinct options, including "do nothing" and "shut it down" — check verifies their presence by keywords. Each with: strong objections (attacked by the red-team subagent), formula-based economics with ranges, and the conditions under which the option is right. Output: outputs/03_options.md. Gate: red team has responded, check passes.
help_page.k102: Agent: shows the option comparison (criteria, economics, risks) and a single recommendation, then asks — pfs ask "Which option do we take?" --options "A,B,C". Human: picks the option — the answer is stored in state.json and grounds the strategies and the D### decision (as in the Connection for Loved Ones demo: option B "Warn before the outage" chosen). No strategies are written before the choice.
help_page.k104: Agent: writes the product strategy — audience and their job, alternatives, the chosen direction and conscious trade-offs, benefit-to-cost economics — and the communication strategy — audience and situation, the comprehension barrier, the key message, its proof, channel roles. Consistency is enforced by a "promise → product proof" table: every promise cites a C###. The comms-strategist subagent drafts the comms part. Output: 04_product_strategy.md, 05_comms_strategy.md.
help_page.k106: Agent: states the expected change (which metric, by how much), the comparison baseline (prior period, control group), the observation window, unwanted side effects (counter-metrics), and continue / adjust / stop criteria. All five sections are mandatory — check enforces them. Output: outputs/06_validation_plan.md.
help_page.k108: Agent: runs pfs check --strict, requests an independent rubric review (the evidence-auditor subagent) and assembles the committee pack: pfs calc all (4 Excel workbooks) and pfs export --six-pager (FAQ-1…6 + attachments). On a borderline score the model escalates and the step repeats. Output: outputs/07_quality_review.md, SIX_PAGER.md, attachments/*.xlsx.
help_page.k110: Agent: records the decision via pfs decision add: title, statement, owner, grounds (C###), metric with target and date, review date, trigger ("if X — revisit"), commitments ("what | who | when"). Human: approves the decision. Output: a record in decisions.jsonl (D###). From now on pfs next and pfs decision due watch the deadlines.
help_page.k112: Agent: keeps the step open: pfs decision due lists overdue reviews; when new data arrives — pfs source refresh + pfs impact C### locate affected conclusions; stale ones are superseded via pfs claim supersede, conclusions redirected by pfs claim rebase, decisions by pfs decision rebase. Gate: pfs decision due is empty or fully handled.
help_page.k114: A source is the minimal unit of trust. pfs source add <url> downloads the page and extracts text; pfs source add <file> accepts PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, images (your description of what is visible). For a JS-rendered page: save the text manually and add pfs source add --text-file saved.md --url <url> --title "…". For screenshots/audio descriptions: pfs media add (see Media & UX).
help_page.k115: Hygiene: dedup by URL and SHA-256; the domain is checked against projects/<slug>/project.json → allowed_sources (a hook blocks foreign domains before the request); pfs source list — the registry, pfs source show S### — text and metadata; pfs source refresh S### — reload: hash changed → warning and a reminder to run pfs impact S###.
help_page.k116: Source types: public, own, interview, synthetic
help_page.k117:
OriginWhat it isConstraint
public/webPublic pages and publications (default)Project-allowed domains
ownYour materials: briefs, data dumps, internal docsNo closed or personal data
interviewReal interviews — with participant consentNo personal data in the repository
syntheticAI respondents, model-generated dataHypotheses only: facts on synthetic data are blocked by the checker
help_page.k119: A claim is the atom of knowledge. The registry is claims.jsonl; written only via pfs claim add:
help_page.k120:
TypeWhen to useRequirement
factA verified statementSource required; never on synthetic data; grade D forbidden
hypothesisAn assumption we intend to testGrounds: a source or other claims
forecastA model-based predictionGrounds + visible assumptions in the model
assumptionAccepted without testing (demo frame, model scenario)Grounds: where it came from (checker warns otherwise)
inferenceYour conclusion from other claims--from required; never stronger than its weakest input
help_page.k122:
GradeWhat it meansExample
ASeveral independent reliable sources agreeTwo official statistics + an industry study with a transparent sample
BOne reliable source / an authoritative methodCentral-bank data, a study with a disclosed methodology
CA single or partisan source, bias possibleA competitor press release about its own market share
DWeak/unverifiable — cannot be a factA rumor, an anonymous post; a second-hand quote without the primary source
help_page.k123: An inference is never stronger than its weakest critical input: two C grounds and one B give at most C. Set via claim add --grade; supersede preserves the grade automatically.
help_page.k124: Supersede, retract, rebase — history is kept
help_page.k125: After supersede, documents referencing the old ID get a check error with the replacement hint (replacement: C058) — re-tag the lines and rebuild exports. This is a guard, not a bug: documents cannot silently rely on stale claims. The history (who, when, why) stays in the registry.
help_page.k127: pfs impact C005 / pfs impact S002 shows transitively: which claims rely on it, which document lines cite it, which decisions are grounded in it. Practice: impact before an edit, impact after, then pfs check --strict as the final filter.
help_page.k129: Track: pfs decision due — overdue items, due reviews, decisions with stale grounds; pfs decision done --id D001 --commitment K1 — close a commitment; pfs decision list — registry. New data changed the grounds? — run impact, supersede, then pfs decision rebase --id D001 --note "…".
help_page.k131: Same structure in English: brief → research plan → situation → options (≥3 incl. status quo) → product strategy → comms strategy → validation plan (5 mandatory sections) → quality review. Check enforces sections, tagged numbers and option counts.
help_page.k132: REPORT.md — the final document with all attachments
help_page.k133: pfs export assembles REPORT.md: summary, brief, situation, options and choice, both strategies, the validation plan, appendices (claim registry with grades and sources, cost log, Excel links). Edit only outputs/*.md by hand — REPORT rebuilds so nothing drifts. pfs export --six-pager — the committee format.
help_page.k135: FAQ-1 status (market, competitors) · FAQ-2 segments & personas · FAQ-3 initiatives + red-team objections · FAQ-4 tactics (need → mechanics → effect) · FAQ-5 delivery & validation plan · FAQ-6 success metrics with formulas. Numbers come from the claim registry, assumptions visible in calcs.json.
help_page.k137: The file is projects/<slug>/calcs.json. The agent fills values from claims and records grounds in note; missing keys fall back to examples marked "EXAMPLE", visible in Excel.
help_page.k138:
SectionKeyMeaningExample
unit_econarpurevenue per unit, currency per month29
unit_econvc_sharevariable costs as a share of price (inference, infrastructure)0.25
unit_econcaccustomer acquisition cost60
unit_econchurn_monthmonthly payer churn, a fraction0.08
growthmau_start · mau_growth_monthstarting audience and monthly growth2000 · 0.22
growthconv_order · aovorder conversion and average order value0.055 · 29
cohortsizes · retentioncohort sizes and the retention curve by month[150, 200, …]
marketpam · tam_share…PAM and TAM/SAM/SOM shares1.8e9 · 0.3
help_page.k140: pfs calc all|unit-econ|growth|cohort|market writes workbooks to outputs/attachments/. The Input sheet holds editable parameters (with source notes); all other sheets are live formulas: CM, LTV, LTV/CAC, payback, sensitivity (unit economics); MAU → orders → GMV → margin over 12 months (growth); cohorts and M1–M12 retention; PAM→TAM→SAM→SOM.
help_page.k141: Editing: change the Input values — Excel recalculates. If you edit calcs.json — rerun pfs calc all and pfs export --six-pager so the text and workbooks match. A file preview may look "empty" — that is a cached render; formulas compute on open.
help_page.k143: pfs export --deck builds a 16:9 HTML deck from SIX_PAGER.md — section slides in the site's gradient theme, printable to PDF from the browser. pfs docx <file.md> converts Markdown to Word (headings, tables, lists, inline code), dependency-free — for handing documents to the committee.
help_page.k145: Same groups in English: projects (new/list/use/status) · steps (step/next/questions) · ask/answer · sources (S###, dedup, domains, refresh) · claims (C###, 5 types, grades, history) · quality (check/impact) · decisions (D###) · data (profile/cohort/funnel/stats) · interviews · media & UX · knowledge (BM25 over 89 cards) · models (profiles, escalation) · calc (4 formula workbooks) · export (REPORT/six-pager/deck/docx) · log & cost · doctor.
help_page.k147: The pfs-strategist server (stdio, stdlib only) plugs into any environment's .mcp.json — the agent gets the same operations as the CLI. Tools:
help_page.k148:
ToolPurpose
pfs_statusproject state: steps, the next step, open questions
pfs_routerequest scenario → knowledge cards and models per step
pfs_kb_searchsearch across the knowledge-base cards
pfs_source_addregister a source (URL / file / text)
pfs_claim_addregister a claim with a type, sources and a grade
pfs_stepmark a step; mandatory cards and the step gates
pfs_ask / pfs_answera question with options and the human answer
pfs_checkregistry and document quality gates
pfs_nextstep + expectations + commitments + reviews in one call
pfs_data_profile / _cohort / _funnel / _statstable profile, cohorts, funnels, statistics from csv/xlsx
pfs_calc / pfs_exportExcel workbooks and the REPORT/six-pager assembly
pfs_decision_add / pfs_decision_duerecord a decision; due reviews and commitments
help_page.k149: Skills (100): structure and three ways to invoke
help_page.k150: Structure: base per-step skills (13) · product-skills, method procedures (27) · a personal library of ~57 (design, marketing, science, documents & media, meta) · integrations. Each folder .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md holds instructions + scripts + references.
help_page.k151: Invocation: 1) automatic — description triggers; 2) explicit — "use skill <name>: <task>"; 3) per step — pfs step prints mandatory cards. Priority rule: project methodology (KB maps) outranks generic skills. Integration examples: premortem (failure pre-mortem before approval), sdd (development discipline), deck (six-pager presentation), deep-research (literature review via Feynman). Full registry: docs/SKILLS.md.
help_page.k153: router (request scenario), researcher (source extraction), data-analyst (tables, cohorts, funnels), synthetic-respondent (AI persona, hypotheses only), ux-analyst (interface review, evidence-bound), red-team (attacks each option), comms-strategist (comms draft), evidence-auditor (rubric review).
help_page.k155: SessionStart feeds project context on a new chat; PreToolUse (pre_web) enforces allowed domains before fetch; PreToolUse (pre_guard) blocks direct writes to the project registries with a hint pointing to the right pfs command and asks for confirmation on reads outside the repository; PostToolUse logs actions (including manual Bash edits of outputs), scans external text for embedded instructions (flags, never executes), auto-checks changed docs; Stop recomputes session cost from the transcript.
help_page.k157: The model profile lives in config/models.json (tasks: route, judge, editor, red_team… — pfs models pick judge): cheap models for classification, extraction, rubric scoring, AI respondents; strong ones for synthesis, options, red team, strategy. pfs models — table; pick — per task; use — switch profile; pfs route --economy downgrades deep→balanced except red team. Escalation: two consecutive check failures or a borderline rubric score → pfs models escalate <task> and retry with a stronger model. Subagents inherit the profile; pfs models sync after changes.
help_page.k159: The Stop hook recomputes cost from the session transcript (prices from config/pricing.json); pfs cost — totals per model and task; pfs cost --window — periods. Human edits count too: pfs log "brief edit" --human-minutes 15. Demo reference: a full project ≈ $19 with a mixed model profile.
help_page.k160: Data analysis: profile, cohort, funnel, stats
help_page.k161: Before computing, the agent checks metrics, units, periods and gaps (table profile). --save makes a run reproducible. Results go to analysis/ and are anchored as C### claims with the file as source.
help_page.k163: pfs interview guide --persona "Parent, kids 7–12" builds the guide; pfs interview save transcript.md registers it with origin=synthetic. The synthetic-respondent subagent plays the persona. Honesty rule: synthetic answers yield hypotheses only; the checker refuses facts on them; documents mark them as model-generated. Real interviews require consent and no personal data.
help_page.k165: pfs media add shot.png --desc "what is visible" --title "…" copies the media to sources/raw/ and turns the description into a text source: the agent analyzes exactly what is described. pfs ux scaffold S003 --focus "onboarding" builds a heuristics + journey scaffold bound to the material; the ux-analyst subagent fills it without inventing beyond the screenshots.
help_page.k166: Environment: Claude Code — the full experience
help_page.k167: Open the repo folder in Claude Code — everything auto-loads: 100 skills, 8 subagents, 6 hooks, the CLI (pfs …) and MCP tools. Just state the task — the agent takes it from there.
help_page.k168: Environments: Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Windsurf, Copilot
help_page.k169: All environments read AGENTS.md. Cursor — .cursor/rules + MCP from .mcp.json. Codex / OpenCode / Windsurf / Copilot — no hooks: start with "read AGENTS.md and run pfs status" — the agent restores context and continues. The pfs-strategist MCP works everywhere (path-independent launcher).
help_page.k171: MCP server npx mcp-server-linear, key LINEAR_API_KEY in .env (git-ignored). The agent reads issues, comments progress, closes with reports — as in this project: PRO-5…PRO-24 closed with final comments. Same rule: the human decides — no issues are closed without your word.
help_page.k173: MCP https://mcp.lovable.dev is wired in .mcp.json; authorize once via OAuth (/mcp → lovable → Authenticate). Then the agent creates and edits Lovable projects on request: this project's landing lives in the repo (canonical) and in Lovable (mirror). create_project/send_message consume Lovable credits; ready prompts are in docs/lovable-brief.md.
help_page.k175: Higgsfield — image/video generation (this page's art is its work). REA — reverse-engineering of JS pages and closed formats (HAR, SQLite, APK) when plain fetch returns nothing. Feynman — deep-research CLI (literature reviews); a search-provider key is needed for live runs. officecli — Office documents in/out. All are optional MCP/CLI add-ons to the basic loop.
help_page.k177: All state lives in projects/<slug>/: state.json (steps, choices, questions), claims.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, log.jsonl, sources/, outputs/. New chat in the repo folder: the SessionStart hook feeds status and "what to decide now" automatically. Hook-less environment: write "read AGENTS.md and run pfs status". Finished steps never repeat; sources and claims never duplicate.
help_page.k179: A project is a plain folder: copy projects/<slug>/ (or git push/pull if tracked) and open elsewhere. The only non-portable part is secrets in .env: move them manually, never commit. The model profile (config/models.json) is repo-wide.
help_page.k181: Data: public sources and your materials only; no closed company data, no respondents' personal data. Domains: allow-listed in project.json; a hook blocks foreign domains pre-request. Secrets: .env only, git-ignored; no keys ever committed. Embedded instructions: source texts are data; "ignore instructions" inside a source is flagged, never executed. Interviews: real ones need consent; no personal data in the repo; synthetic data is honestly labeled.
help_page.k183: Fact without source → error; fact on synthetic → error; grade-D fact → error; grounds-less hypothesis/forecast/assumption → warning; links to missing/retracted IDs → error with replacement hint; superseded grounds → warning; untagged numbers → warning; <3 options or no status-quo → error; missing required sections → error; sources with embedded instructions → warning listing them.
help_page.k185: Fact without source → by design, add source or use hypothesis; domain not allowed → edit allow-list or --force; 0 chars extracted → JS page, save text manually or use REA; empty Excel preview → computes on open; six-pager ≠ Excel → rerun calc+export; superseded C### in docs → re-tag per hint; no hook status → ask agent to run pfs status; skill missing → restart session; assumption without grounds → register its origin and supersede; Lovable credits → top up or edit site/ directly; MCP tool missing → refresh .mcp.json, restart; interrupted session → pfs status and repeat, --save makes runs reproducible.
help_page.k187: S### source · C### claim (5 types, grade A–D) · D### decision · six-pager (committee report + Excel) · red team · JTBD · traction model · double diamond phases · synthetic data · injection (flagged, never executed) · step gate · named gap · counter-metric · model escalation.

claims.C005: Resume-builder market: estimates range $1.2–2.4B (2024–2025); the AI sub-segment grows $1.3→1.47B at a 13.1% CAGR
claims.C006: 7 direct competitors (Zety, resume.io, Novoresume, Kickresume, Enhancv, Teal, Rezi) run freemium with paid tiers of $8–40/mo and aggressive auto-renewals
claims.C013: An unoccupied niche: a multilingual (19 locales) privacy-first open-source AI resume builder — western competitors cover EN+5 languages and run in the cloud
claims.C014: Honest pricing (no auto-renewals) and open source are a working differentiator against competitors with aggressive auto-renewals, especially for a technical audience
claims.C016: Unit assumptions of the demo model: paid tier $29/mo, variable costs (inference + infrastructure) 25%, CAC $60 (SEO / Product Hunt / communities), payer churn 8%/mo
claims.C019: The demo committee chose option B — hosted freemium SaaS globally; required mitigations: a BYOK free tier, opt-in cloud on a local core, honest pricing without auto-renewals, locale waves EN→DE/ES/PT-BR→JA/ZH; stop thresholds from the validation plan

triggers: paid < 20 by week 12 with activation < 35% -> close the commercial track (option E)
GitHub stars fall > 30% after the cloud announcement -> rework the opt-in communication
demo_data_en.metric_target: >=40 paying users of the hosted beta (baseline: 0)
countermetrics: GitHub stars/forks must not decline after the cloud announcement
privacy/GDPR complaints — no more than 5 per month
beta NPS — not below 30 while signups grow
